sources.news_title: US Intelligence Sharing Resumes After Pause, Zelenskyy Says
sources.text:
The United States has resumed its sharing of important intelligence with Ukraine to help defend the country against Russia, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
Zelenskyy said on NBC’s “Meet The Press” on Sunday that the United States has “unique intelligence” to alert Ukraine of ballistic attacks and Ukraine didn’t get that intelligence for three days.
“We are very thankful for this,” Zelenskyy said. “Now it works.”
Separately, Zelenskyy also said in the interview that a restriction on Starlink satellite internet that disrupted Ukrainian combat missions and threatened defenses against Russian drones was a “message” from America’s government.
Ukraine’s defense forces received no advance notice, he said, and several missions were disrupted.
Starlink supports battlefield communications and drones used to attack Russian targets. Beskrestnov said the restrictions also affected frontline logistics and interceptor drones that Ukraine uses against fast-moving, jet-powered Russian Shahed drones.
He described those interceptors as the most effective available means of countering the aircraft and warned that the restrictions undermined Ukraine’s air defenses.
Beskrestnov alleged that the change was politically motivated but provided no evidence and didn’t identify who might have requested it.
Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski challenged SpaceX CEO Elon Musk on X, asking whether the restrictions were intended to exert political pressure on Ukraine. Poland has previously said it pays for Ukraine’s Starlink subscription.
Alexander Beglov, the governor of St. Petersburg, reported on Sunday that his region was hit by Ukrainian drones that killed one and injured five. Beglov said 12 apartment buildings and two private homes were damaged and the Petersburg Oil Terminal, the Ruchyi oil depot, and industrial warehouses in the Kolpino district were also attacked. There were fires at the Petersburg Oil Terminal.
Trump has expressed frustration with Zelenskyy’s targeting Russian refineries, which Trump has said is a major reason the cost of diesel fuel has increased around the world.
Zelenskyy “has to do one thing—he has to stop knocking out diesel fuel in Russia,” Trump said to reporters at the Irish Open. “There are plenty of other targets. Don’t hit diesel fuel, because that’s hurting the world.”
On Oct. 10, Trump said that he told Zelenskyy, “‘You can do whatever you want to Russia, but don’t hit the refineries because that’s a world problem.’ … And what does he do? He goes and hits the diesel fuel.”
Diesel in the United States has climbed from $3.63 a gallon a year ago to $6.32 on average as of Oct. 18, according to AAA.
The agreement, which followed a telephone conversation with Russian President Vladimir Putin, would help lower fuel prices for Americans—particularly farmers, ranchers, and truckers—Trump said.
The planned shipments to be added to the American and global markets include more than 300,000 tons immediately, another 500,000 tons in November, and a million tons in December, Trump said. Russia could supply another 3 million tons beginning next year, depending on the condition of its refineries.
Putin said Russia was prepared to supply oil and petroleum products to American and international buyers, describing the agreement as beneficial to the global economy.
Zelenskyy criticized the agreement and urged stronger sanctions against Russia. He said easing sanctions without a clear, lasting agreement to de-escalate the war would demonstrate weakness toward Moscow.
The Ukrainian president said on “Meet The Press” that it was a “very bad surprise” to hear from the media about the Russia–U.S. diesel deal.

sources.news_title: US resumes intel sharing on Russian missile launches with Ukraine, Zelensky says
sources.text:
US resumes intel sharing on Russian missile launches with Ukraine, Zelensky says
The United States has resumed sharing intelligence about incoming Russian ballistic missiles with Ukraine after a pause lasting several days, President Volodymyr Zelensky told NBC News' "Meet the Press" in an interview published on Oct. 18.
"Only the United States has this unique intelligence to tell our side when Russia uses ballistic missiles. We didn't receive it during ballistic attacks for three days," Zelensky said.
The U.S. provides Ukraine with intelligence to help its military detect and track Russian missile launches and other aerial threats. Zelensky said the issue had since been resolved and thanked Washington for restoring intelligence sharing.
"We are very thankful for this," he said. "Now it works."
At the same time, he said Ukraine was still experiencing an ongoing speed restriction on its use of Starshield — the militarized version of SpaceX's Starlink satellite internet system
Asked whether U.S. President Donald Trump or SpaceX CEO Elon Musk had personally ordered the restrictions, Zelensky said he did not know but believed "both" were involved. He added that if Trump decided to lift the restrictions, the service would return to its previous state.
read also
The resumption of intelligence sharing follows a Russian missile attack on Kyiv on Oct. 12, when five Russian S-400 missiles struck the Ukrainian capital, causing "massive explosions." Air raid sirens and mobile alerts sounded only after the attack.
A senior Ukrainian official previously told the Kyiv Independent that Ukraine's military leadership contacted its U.S. counterparts after the strike to clarify what had happened.
"They say they didn't cut it off, but they didn't warn us (about the attack) either," the official said. "The Americans said they just didn't see (the launch)... That's a weak excuse."
The incident came amid broader tensions over U.S. support for Ukraine. The Kyiv Independent earlier learned that the Trump administration had threatened senior Ukrainian military and government officials in a push to protect Russian oil refineries.
Zelensky also told NBC that if thet U.S. chooses to support Russia over Kyiv, consequences would be dire — for both the Ukraine and the United States.
Such a move would be a "historic mistake" for Washington, Zelensky said. A U.S-Russia alliance would also destroy Ukraine's chances of defending itself against the full-scale invasion.
"“If these two countries will be together ... we will not prevail, and we will not be able to stand," Zelensky warned.
But the president also expressed hope that talks with the U.S. could take place next week, despite the ongoing difficulties between Kyiv and Washington.
"I'm very open to this, even with all the difficult circumstances," he said, estimating that a meeting could take place on Oct. 20-21.
Zelensky also denounced Kremlin narratives — sometimes repeated by Trump — that he opposes democratic elections in Ukraine.
If the U.S. and Russia believe Ukraine must hold elections during wartime, Moscow must grant Kyiv an unconditional ceasefire for 60 days, he said. The president said he made it clear that a minimum of 60 days was necessary for Ukraine to change its laws, prepare election infrastructure, and guarantee soldiers the opportunity to vote.
"If you think that I don't want elections, it's not true, and it's not fair," he said.
Zelensky said he would run for office again if elections were held during wartime, citing a responsibility to continue defending his country.

sources.news_title: Zelensky tells NBC 'thankful' US has unblocked intelligence sharing
sources.text:
Zelensky tells NBC 'thankful' US has unblocked intelligence sharing
Washington (United States) (AFP) – Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he was "thankful" that the United States has resumed intelligence sharing after a pause had left his country more vulnerable to Russian missile strikes.
Issued on: Modified:
"It was blocked for some period of time. And then it was deblocked by the American side. We are very thankful for this. Now it works," Zelensky told NBC's "Meet the Press" in an interview published on Sunday.
"Only (the) United States has this unique intelligence to tell our side when Russia uses ballistic missiles. And we didn't get it during ballistic attacks during three days," Zelensky added.
In the past week, Kyiv also reported restrictions to satellite services operated by Elon Musk's SpaceX, which Ukraine relies on for battlefield communications, shortly after US President Donald Trump criticized Ukraine and urged it to stop targeting Russian oil refineries.
Zelensky said he believed "it was a message from American government to limit the speed. And technically, SpaceX did it."
The Trump administration has denied it was behind any slowdown, and Zelensky's remark drew a quick rebuke from a top US official.
"President (Donald) Trump and Secretary (of State Marco) Rubio have categorically said that no one in the Trump administration did that. And I think it is very reckless for President Zelensky to make such a charge," Bessent told NBC in a separate interview aired on the same show Sunday.
Bessent did not provide an alternative explanation.
Musk, who has himself been critical of Zelensky and has called on him "to go," said on Wednesday that any disruptions reported by Ukraine in using the Starshield satellite communications system would be the responsibility of the US government.
Zelensky told NBC it would be "a historic mistake" if the United States formally supports Russia, which launched an invasion of Ukraine in 2022. But he said he believes his country retains bipartisan support in Washington and that he still views Trump as an ally.
"We want to trust him, and I hope that he will change his decisions," the Ukrainian leader said of the US president. "Because I think that it's all mistakes and it will not help us. And it will not help United States."
In another setback to Kyiv, Trump on Friday signed an executive order that waived sweeping sanctions and tariffs targeting Russia -- measures adopted by Congress last month.
Top US diplomat Rubio on Saturday described that as a 60-day pause to "analyze" the impact on the global economy.
The waiver came after Trump struck a deal with Putin to allow exports of Russian diesel, a move intended to ease fuel prices in the United States ahead of midterm elections next month.
Zelensky said waiving sanctions was "strengthening (Vladimir) Putin's war against us" -- referring to the Russian president -- and if Washington officially takes Moscow's side, "It's a historic mistake and a big tragedy."

sources.news_title: Zelensky Says US Intelligence Sharing Resumes After Ukraine ‘Blinded’ to Russian Attacks
sources.text:
WASHINGTON — President Volodymyr Zelensky said the United States has resumed sharing intelligence with Ukraine after a roughly three-day disruption that left Kyiv with less warning of incoming Russian attacks.
Zelensky welcomed the restoration of the intelligence pipeline, saying the interruption had weakened Ukraine’s ability to prepare for Russian strikes before it was lifted.
“It was blocked for some period of time. And then it was de-blocked by the American side. We are very thankful for this. Now it works,” Zelensky told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” in a prerecorded interview broadcast Sunday.
“We didn’t see attacks of Russia using ballistic missiles,” Zelensky said. “We have dozens of countries who help. But only United States has this unique intelligence to tell our side when Russia uses ballistic missiles. And we didn’t get it during ballistic attacks during three days.”
Ukraine has made significant progress in defending against Russian drones while also expanding its own drone operations against targets inside Russia.
Ballistic missiles, however, remain a far more difficult threat. Ukraine has struggled to intercept them, in part because of a shortage of Patriot air-defense interceptors that reportedly was recently exhausted.
The intelligence disruption came as tensions escalated between Kyiv and Washington over Ukrainian strikes against Russia’s energy infrastructure. President Trump has blamed those attacks for contributing to higher diesel prices, a politically sensitive issue as the midterm elections approach.
YOU MIGHT ALSO LIKE: Shocking Tiger Attack: Man Dies in Wildlife Park Incident – VIDEO
Trump announced an energy ceasefire in Ukraine last week, catching Kyiv off guard. Ukrainian officials said they paused attacks on Russian energy facilities for several days, but resumed them after Russia continued striking Ukraine’s own energy sites.
“If you tell me that Zelensky is again shooting at refineries, all he’s doing is making the world oil price higher,” Trump told Newsmax host Rob Finnerty on Thursday. “I think that’s a disgrace. There’s plenty of other targets.”
Ukraine has also alleged that its access to Starlink’s military service was restricted. Kyiv said the move reduced its ability to track and intercept drone attacks and to conduct drone strikes against Russian targets.
Officials have offered conflicting accounts of who ordered the reported throttling and whether Ukraine’s access to the satellite internet network has been completely restored.
Asked why Trump appears more willing to speak favorably about Russian President Vladimir Putin than about him, Zelensky suggested the difference may stem from his own direct approach.
“I’m very honest with the President of the United States, and very clear, and very supportive of America because we are strategic partners,” Zelensky said. “He’s [Putin] a killer.”
“That’s why I’m very honest and open to say that he’s a killer,” he added. “But I’m better to have partners who are very open and clear than to have those who are killers, even with a smile on their face.”

Zelensky reveals US intel sharing is back after blackout left Ukraine blind to Russian attacks
WASHINGTON — President Volodymyr Zelensky revealed that US intelligence sharing with Ukraine is back on after a blackout left the country blind to incoming Russian attacks.
Zelensky expressed gratitude that the lull in intelligence sharing, which lasted about three days and undermined Ukraine’s ability to prepare for the attacks, has since ended.
“It was blocked for some period of time. And then it was de-blocked by the American side. We are very thankful for this. Now it works,” Zelensky told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” in a prerecorded interview that aired Sunday.
“We didn’t see attacks of Russia using ballistic missiles,” Zelensky explained. “We have dozens of countries who help. But only United States has this unique intelligence to tell our side when Russia uses ballistic missiles. And we didn’t get it during ballistic attacks during three days.”
Ukraine has made remarkable advancements in its ability to both combat Russian drones and carry out drone attacks of its own.
But it has long struggled to counter Russian ballistic missiles, particularly due to a shortage of Patriot interceptors, which reportedly ran out recently.
The pause in intelligence sharing came amid a feud between Kyiv and Washington over Ukraine’s attacks on Russia’s energy infrastructure, which President Trump has blamed for rising diesel prices, something that has given him headaches in the midterms.
Last week, Trump declared an energy ceasefire in Ukraine, which caught Kyiv by surprise. Ukraine claimed it halted attacks on Russian energy targets for several days in response. But because Russia continued to bombard its energy sites, Ukraine resumed those attacks.
“If you tell me that Zelensky is again shooting at refineries, all he’s doing is making the world oil price higher,” Trump vented to Newsmax host Rob Finnerty on Thursday. “I think that’s a disgrace. There’s plenty of other targets.”
In addition to the alleged intelligence blackout, Ukraine also claimed that its access to a military version of Starlink was throttled, which limited its ability to intercept drone attacks and carry out drone strikes on Russia.
There are conflicting claims of who ordered the throttling of Ukraine’s access to that satellite internet system and whether or not it has been fully restored.
When asked about why Trump appears to have kinder words to say about Russian tyrant Vladimir Putin than himself, Zelensky reflected that it may be related to his bluntness.
“I’m very honest with the President of the United States, and very clear, and very supportive of America because we are strategic partners,” he said. “He’s [Putin] a killer.”
“That’s why I’m very honest and open to say that he’s a killer,” he added. “But I’m better to have partners who are very open and clear than to have those who are killers, even with a smile on their face.”

sources.news_title: US Resumes Intelligence Sharing With Ukraine, Zelensky Says
sources.text:
The US has resumed sharing military and security intelligence with Ukraine after suspending data exchanges for a “some period of time,” President Volodymyr Zelensky announced on Sunday, Oct. 18.
Speaking during an interview on NBC’s “Meet the Press,” as reported by Bloomberg, the president confirmed that intelligence pipelines had been restored following operational friction with Washington.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
Zelensky also expressed hope that bilateral negotiations with American officials could take place within the coming week.
Warnings over energy interdiction and early-warning gaps
The temporary suspension of intelligence flows materialized amid sharp disagreements between Washington and Kyiv over battlefield targeting rules and prospective ceasefire mechanisms.
On Oct. 15, The Washington Post reported that US intelligence officials warned Ukraine that Washington would immediately halt intelligence sharing if Ukrainian forces continued long-range strikes against Russian oil refineries and petrochemical facilities.
The warning was formally conveyed to Ukraine’s embassy in Washington amid disputes surrounding an “energy ceasefire” unilaterally declared by US President Donald Trump.
The Trump administration had previously cautioned that it could suspend intelligence cooperation and block European purchases of American weapons earmarked for Ukraine if Kyiv refused to halt deep interdiction strikes on Russian energy infrastructure.
US Goes on the Offensive in Central Asia
While American sources cited by The Washington Post maintained that intelligence sharing was never completely dismantled, they acknowledged that specific data feeds had been restricted.
Prior to the restoration, Zelensky disclosed that Ukrainian defense forces received no advance warnings from Western partners regarding Russian ballistic missile launches toward Kyiv for two consecutive nights, during which kinetic impacts damaged critical capital energy installations and knocked out municipal power and water grids.
Bilateral coordination
Zelensky’s confirmation that intelligence sharing has resumed comes as Ukrainian and American officials work to arrange direct bilateral consultations.
On Friday, Oct. 16, National Security and Defense Council Secretary Rustem Umerov held consultations with US special envoy Jared Kushner to discuss a timetable and format for upcoming in-person meetings.
Zelensky affirmed that Kyiv remains prepared for direct discussions with White House representatives to explore verifiable mechanisms for a reciprocal energy armistice to protect civilian utility networks ahead of winter.
The restoration of intelligence sharing also coincides with public scrutiny over related technological restrictions affecting Ukrainian defense capabilities, including artificial speed limitations placed on commercial Starlink terminals and Ukraine’s lack of access to the Pentagon-contracted Starshield satellite network.

sources.news_title: U.S. resumes intelligence-sharing with Ukraine after pause, Zelenskyy says
sources.text:
U.S. resumes intelligence-sharing with Ukraine after pause, Zelenskyy says
The United States has resumed providing Ukraine critical intelligence to help it defend against Russian missile strikes, after a brief pause, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in comments published on Sunday.
Ukraine has relied on US intelligence to spot the fast-moving ballistic missiles that Russia has fired in waves at its cities. US President Donald Trump had said earlier this week that Washington was still sharing intelligence, although Ukrainian officials said some Russian strikes had occurred without warning.
Speaking to NBC’s Meet the Press, Zelenskyy said intelligence-sharing had been interrupted but later “de-blocked.”
“We are very thankful for this,” he said. “Now it works.”
But Zelenskyy said other US actions, such as signing a deal to import Russian diesel and waiving sanctions on Russia that had been slated to take effect this week, will hurt Ukraine.
“If the United States will officially take the side of Russia, of course if these two countries will be together, of course we will not prevail and we will not be able to stand,” he said.
Over the past week, a widening rift between Trump and Zelenskyy has sparked concerns that their tumultuous relationship could lead to even worse outcomes for Kyiv. Zelenskyy told NBC that he hopes Trump will remain an ally of Ukraine.
“We want to trust him, and I hope that he will change his decisions,” Zelenskyy said. “Because I think that it’s all mistakes and it will not help us. And it will not help United States.”
In a Truth Social post on Sunday afternoon, Trump wrote that his decision-making was aimed at avoiding anything “that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table.”
Ukraine gets US help that Russia does not receive, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told NBC, citing intelligence-sharing and the provision of US munitions to other countries for resale to Ukraine.
But Bessent, speaking with “Meet the Press” after it aired Zelenskyy’s interview, did not directly answer when asked multiple times whether the United States views Ukraine as an ally.
“Zelenskyy presents a false binary this morning that Ukraine must win,” Bessent said. “The war must end, and that will be with some kind of a negotiated settlement.”
(Reporting by Dan Peleschuk and Michael Derby; Editing by Joe Bavier, Sergio Non and Edmund Klamann)

sources.news_title: Zelensky: The US has resumed giving intelligence on Russian ballistic missiles – “For three days we received nothing”
sources.text:
The United States has resumed giving Ukraine information on Russian ballistic missile launches, after an interruption of about three days. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said so in an interview on NBC’s “Meet the Press” broadcast on Sunday, October 18. “Only the United States has this unique information, to inform our side when Russia uses ballistic missiles. We were not receiving it during ballistic attacks for three days,” he said. “We are very grateful for this. Now it works,” he added.
According to NBC, Zelensky described the information flow as briefly “blocked”, leaving Ukraine “blind” against ballistic missiles, while limits were also placed on Starlink technology, which is critical for shooting down jet drones. The Ukrainian president said Kyiv believes SpaceX’s decision to limit the speed came after a “message from the US government”. The restriction on Starshield, the military version of Starlink, remains in force. Already on October 16 he had written that when the speed was cut, Ukraine could not shoot down some Shahed jets.
The restoration comes after the Russian attack of October 12 on Kyiv, when five S-400 missiles struck the capital and the sirens sounded only after the explosions. Zelensky had also warned of Russian plans to deploy ballistic missiles in Belarus for strikes on western Ukraine.
“A historic mistake”
In the same interview, the Ukrainian president said it would be a “historic mistake” if the US sided with Putin. “If these two countries are together, we will not prevail and we will not be able to hold out,” he said. Of Donald Trump he said: “We want to trust him. I hope he will change his decisions, because I think they are all mistakes.” Responding to Trump’s remark that he is a harder negotiating partner than Putin, he said it is “better to have partners who are very open and clear, than those who are killers, even with a smile on their face.” The interview was given two days after the Trump administration froze new sanctions against Russia.
Later on Sunday, Zelensky announced that he had spoken with the envoys of the American president, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. “Peace comes only through strength and cooperation built on trust,” he wrote. Zelensky said talks with the US could take place next week. There has been no official US statement on the interruption or the restoration of the information flow.

“Only (the) United States has this unique intelligence to tell our side when Russia uses ballistic missiles. And we didn’t get it during ballistic attacks during three days,” Zelenskyy added.
In the past week, Kyiv also reported restrictions to satellite services operated by Elon Musk’s SpaceX, which Ukraine relies on for battlefield communications, shortly after US President Donald Trump criticised Ukraine and urged it to stop targeting Russian oil refineries.
Zelenskyy said he believed “it was a message from American government to limit the speed. And technically, SpaceX did it.”
The Trump administration has denied it was behind any slowdown, and Zelenskyy’s remark drew a quick rebuke from a top US official.
“President (Donald) Trump and Secretary (of State Marco) Rubio have categorically said that no one in the Trump administration did that. And I think it is very reckless for President Zelenskyy to make such a charge,” Bessent told NBC in a separate interview aired on the same show Sunday.
Bessent did not provide an alternative explanation.
Musk, who has himself been critical of Zelenskyy and has called on him “to go,” said on Wednesday that any disruptions reported by Ukraine in using the Starshield satellite communications system would be the responsibility of the US government.
Zelenskyy told NBC it would be “a historic mistake” if the United States formally supports Russia, which launched an invasion of Ukraine in 2022. But he said he believes his country retains bipartisan support in Washington and that he still views Trump as an ally.
“We want to trust him, and I hope that he will change his decisions,” the Ukrainian leader said of the US president. “Because I think that it’s all mistakes and it will not help us. And it will not help United States.”
In another setback to Kyiv, Trump on Friday signed an executive order that waived sweeping sanctions and tariffs targeting Russia, measures adopted by Congress last month.
Top US diplomat Rubio on Saturday described that as a 60-day pause to “analyse” the impact on the global economy.
The waiver came after Trump struck a deal with Putin to allow exports of Russian diesel, a move intended to ease fuel prices in the United States ahead of midterm elections next month.
Zelenskyy said waiving sanctions was “strengthening (Vladimir) Putin’s war against us”, referring to the Russian president, and if Washington officially takes Moscow’s side, “It’s a historic mistake and a big tragedy.”

sources.news_title: ZELENSKYY SAYS U.S. INTELLIGENCE SHARING HAS RESUMED AFTER INTERRUPTION
sources.text:
ZELENSKYY SAYS U.S. INTELLIGENCE SHARING HAS RESUMED AFTER INTERRUPTION
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says the United States is again sharing intelligence with Ukraine after an interruption lasting “a certain period of time.”
Speaking to NBC, in remarks reported by Bloomberg, he also expressed hope that talks with Washington could take place soon.
The announcement follows days of Ukrainian objections, European concern, and bipartisan criticism in Washington over the administration’s approach to Russia. The restoration is an important development, although what prompted it has not been publicly established.
For Ukraine, intelligence cooperation is a matter of survival. Kyiv had reported missing warnings about Russian ballistic missile launches—information that can give defenders and civilians precious time to respond. Restoring that cooperation matters far beyond the diplomatic headlines.
The wider dispute has exposed the consequences of treating Ukraine’s security as leverage. Washington’s pressure over Ukrainian refinery strikes, its diesel agreement with Moscow, and relief from sanctions have drawn resistance from people who see the danger of rewarding Russia while demanding restraint from the country it invaded.
The United States remains enormously powerful. But Ukraine has its own voice, European partners have their own security interests, and American lawmakers can challenge decisions made by their administration. Those voices cannot simply be brushed aside.
Renewed intelligence sharing is a necessary step. It must now be followed by reliable cooperation and diplomacy that respects Ukraine’s right to defend itself and determine its future. 
A country fighting for survival deserves more than uncertainty over whether vital support will still be there tomorrow.

sources.news_title: U.S. Resumes Critical Intelligence Support to Ukraine Amid Tensions
sources.text:
U.S. Resumes Critical Intelligence Support to Ukraine Amid Tensions
The United States has restarted its critical intelligence support to Ukraine, enabling the country to defend against Russian missile attacks, according to President Volodymyr Zelensky.
Ukraine has relied on U.S. intelligence to detect high-speed ballistic missiles launched by Russia towards its cities.
During an appearance on NBC’s “Meet the Press,” Zelensky noted that the exchange of information had been interrupted but has since been “unblocked.”
“We are very grateful for this,” he stated. “Now it is functioning.”
President Donald Trump indicated earlier this week that Washington continues to provide intelligence, despite claims from Ukrainian officials that some Russian attacks occurred without warning.
The resumption of vital intelligence comes amid heightened tensions following Ukraine’s long-range strikes on Russian oil refineries, as reported by The Kyiv Post.
According to The Washington Post, U.S. intelligence officials warned Ukraine that the information exchange would be halted immediately if Ukrainian forces continued their distant attacks against Russian oil refineries and petrochemical facilities.
The Trump administration had previously cautioned that it might suspend intelligence cooperation and block European purchases of U.S. arms intended for Ukraine if Kyiv refused to cease such strikes, which the president indicated were contributing to rising fuel prices.

The United States has resumed providing Ukraine with critical intelligence to help defend against Russian missile strikes after a brief pause, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said in comments published on Sunday.
Ukraine has relied on US intelligence to spot the fast-moving ballistic missiles that Russia has fired in waves at its cities.
Speaking to NBC’s Meet the Press, Zelenskiy said intelligence-sharing had been interrupted but later “de-blocked”.
“We are very thankful for this,” he said. “Now it works.
“US President Donald Trump had said earlier this week that Washington was still sharing intelligence, despite Ukrainian officials saying some Russian strikes had occurred without warning.

sources.news_title: Zelensky Confirms US Has Resumed Intelligence Sharing
sources.text:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has said the United States is once again sharing intelligence after the process was paused for a period.
The Ukrainian leader said this on Sunday in an interview with NBC, Bloomberg reports.
Zelensky also expressed hope that talks with the United States would take place as early as this week.
- Recently, Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said that Ukraine continues to receive intelligence from the United States.
- It was previously reported that US officials stepped up pressure on Ukraine, demanding it stop strikes on Russian oil refineries, otherwise threatening to halt the transfer of intelligence.
- The Financial Times wrote that last week Ukraine’s negotiating team met with Trump representatives in Miami for almost eight hours. The sides were expected to discuss ways to persuade Russia to end the war.
- The US administration has already suspended intelligence sharing with Ukraine: in March 2025, cooperation was halted for eight days after a dispute between Trump and Zelensky.
- On the evening of 12 October this year, the Russian army used missiles against Kyiv. The first explosions were heard even before the air-raid siren. Afterwards, Zelensky said Ukraine had not received a warning from partners about the missile attack on Kyiv.
- Restrictions on Starlink’s operation were also recorded. The military reported on the morning of 14 October that service had been cut off at speeds of 160 km/h. This disrupted some planned missions and created difficulties in repelling Russian drone attacks. SpaceX founder Elon Musk said the decision on restrictions is made by the US government.
